method: A deterministic, geometric read of about one year of daily bars plus weekly context; no AI vision. Swing points come from an ATR directional-change zigzag confirmed on the close, and each swing carries the date it became known, so nothing uses hindsight. Trendlines are exact: the edge of the convex hull of the confirmed swing lows (or highs) on log price, touched but never crossed; a break needs a close more than 0.25 ATR beyond the line. Support/resistance zones come from three separate sources, each named: clustered swing points, a volume- and recency-weighted price histogram, and round numbers; touch counts and ages are facts, never weights. Triangles, wedges and channels are the envelope lines of the latest swings, with the apex where they meet. Every named pattern must also look like its name or it is not shown: flat edges drift at most 1 ATR, each edge has at least 2 touches spread across the pattern, triangle and wedge edges converge with the apex ahead, no gap over 2.5 ATR or lone impulse leg sits inside it, and most closes stay between the lines. Candlesticks count only within 0.25 ATR of a measured level. Structure (lost rising support or last swing low, confirmed by a close under the 50-day) follows the desk's structural screen written after the SNDK breakdown of 2026-10-12. Divergences compare RSI(14) and MACD (in ATR units) at confirmed swings 5 to 60 sessions apart; RSI and MACD agreeing count once. Volume is measured against the 50-session median, and a breakout is called volume-confirmed at 1.5x or more, otherwise 'unconfirmed by volume', never 'failed'. Fibonacci levels are measured on the one-year swing and are context, not forecasts. Stages lead with the 30-week average (rising or falling, price above or below); the Weinstein stage number is secondary. Projected levels: a confirmed pattern's measured move (its height from the breakout level, Bulkowski), the swing measured move (AB=CD) and the 1.272 / 1.618 Fibonacci extensions of the one-year swing; each card shows how often past trades of its strategy reached such a level. The read can only warn or demote; it never adds points, and it is logged before outcomes so each item can be tested.
